market_holds: Spot $19.20 at the sealed close (baseline 2026-11-19), 4.2% above the 52-week low and 33% below the high. Run-up is flat: +1.6% over 5 sessions, -0.2% over 20. No usable option chain, so the baseline's expected move is the 2.28% median of 8 prior reactions, which understates a recent -14.3% on the 2026-08-07 Q3 print (guide cut). The stock is down about 18% since that report (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-11). FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide is $158-162M (cut in August from at least $180M), which against nine-month adjusted EBITDA of $114.955M implies Q4 of $43.0-47.0M, against $35.0M in Q3 and $51.5M in Q4 FY25. Management targeted about $175M for full-year Memorialization, which implies about $45M in Q4. Q4 consensus is adjusted EPS $0.28 on revenue of $254.1M (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11). FY26 EPS consensus is $0.51 and FY27 is $0.78 (+53%), from 3 analysts whose targets were last updated 2026-08-21 (stockanalysis.com), so the forward estimates are stale. Short interest is 5.09M shares at 2026-10-30, about 16% of roughly 31M shares and 10.2 days to cover, nearly double the 2.65M at 2026-07-31 (Nasdaq). Covenant relief since 2026-09-01 allows leverage up to 5.25x. The board raised the dividend to $0.26 (33rd straight raise) on 2026-11-18. A new CEO, Whitehead, was appointed 2026-08-11, so this is his first print. The call is 09:00 ET on 11-20, before the scored open.
view: This is a new CEO's first print. It comes at the bottom of the range, with a heavy and growing short base and a guide that was cut once already. The Q4 EBITDA line is more likely to land at or below the low end of $158-162M than in the middle. Copper cost is the main reason. Matthews buys about six months forward, so Q4 bronze cost reflects January-March 2026 copper (about $12,800/t on FRED) against about $11,100/t for Q3's cost basis, a step-up of roughly 15%. Management said in August that costs had 'materially outpaced' price increases and that further price actions would come 'later in the calendar year', which is after this quarter. Volumes help a little: SCI's comparable funeral services went from -1% in Q2 to -0.1% in Q3 2026, and Matthews said July was better. Industrial Technologies lost $5.4M in Q3, and energy storage delays run through the year. My build (Memorialization 43-45, Brand/Propelis about 10, Industrial Tech -3 to 0, corporate about -11.5) gives roughly $40-43M against the $43-47M the guide needs. The line the stock will actually trade on, though, is probably the FY27 framing. Stale consensus has EPS up 53%, and Matthews has missed its own annual guide in consecutive years. A new CEO has every incentive to set a low bar or not give a number, which leans negative. Against that: the stock already sits near its post-Q3 low, short interest is about 16% of shares, and the board raised the dividend the day before the release, which argues against a balance-sheet shock. An engineering-business sale, under review 'through the fourth quarter', or a firm Propelis exit plan could also land in the release and squeeze the shorts. Net, I lean modestly down, nowhere near a bettable edge.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the Q4 bronze margin squeeze from lagged copper costs, plus the stale FY27 EPS consensus (+53%, last revised in August), which a new CEO's first outlook is likely to undercut. Neither can be shown to be priced; the August-dated estimates have not visibly moved. But the 16% short interest and the price near its lows mean some of this downside is already positioned for. The gap is small and uncertain.

recommendation.reason: The inputs lean toward Q4 adjusted EBITDA at or below the low end of guidance, because lagged copper costs rise and price increases come after the quarter, and toward a conservative first FY27 frame from a new CEO against stale +53% EPS estimates. But the stock is near its lows with about 16% of shares short and 10 days to cover, the board just raised the dividend, and a strategic transaction could land in the release. The direction probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An announced sale of the engineering business or a dated Propelis exit with debt paydown, or an FY27 EBITDA guide at or above the Street, which into a 16% short base would gap the stock up.

self_critique: The guide was set in early August, with July already known and Q4 being 'seasonally one of our best quarters'. A company cutting with one quarter left usually sets a reachable number, so Q4 may well land inside the range. The stock has already de-rated 18% since that cut, with short interest nearly doubled, so a merely in-line print plus any concrete portfolio step (engineering sale, Propelis exit, debt target) could squeeze it up hard. A new CEO may also simply skip FY27 guidance, which removes my main negative line. The dividend raise the day before shows the board is not worried about cash.
approach_notes: The P6 instruction to find the line and P4's warning not to treat a drawdown as cushion helped frame the guide arithmetic and the FY27 question. The P3 'counterparties first' route paid through SCI's funeral volumes and FRED copper. With no option chain and stale consensus, P7's three-part gate kept this from becoming a forced call.
